question: Which visa applicants have to submit a tuberculosis test certificate at a Korean diplomatic mission?
reference: Nationals of high TB-burden countries who live in one of those countries and apply for a long-term visa (stay of 91 days or longer) at a diplomatic mission.
answer:
Nationals of high TB-burden countries living in those countries who apply for a long-term visa (stay period of 91 days or longer) at a diplomatic mission must submit the certificate [2]. This requirement applies to nationals such as Chinese citizens living in China or Thailand, but not to nationals like Chinese citizens living in the U.S. [2].

Answer covers only applicants submitting at a diplomatic mission for long-term visas from high TB-burden countries; it does not specify requirements for other visa types, entry points, or dates outside the March 2016 context.

passages.title: Introducing declaration of accommodation by short-term foreign residents
passages.snippet:
by short-term foreign residents
went into force as of 10 December 2020
as a measure to prevent the spread of communicable disease in the country
This schemes aims to minimise social/economic loss and ensure safety of the public by locating short-term residents' accommodation in a timely manner should a communicable disease outbreak or a terrorist attack takes place.
Declaration is required in the issuance of a crisis alert* of the "interest" level or higher in line with "Infectious Disease Control And Prevention Act" or
in the issuance of a crisis alert* of the "caution" level of higher
in line with "Act On Counter-terrorism For The Protection Of Citizens And Public Security".
* Alerts are classified into four levels, namely: attention, caution, alert, and serious.
Foreign residents holding short-term visas- B-1(Visa exempted), B-2(Tourism/transit), C-1(Short-term news coverage), C-3(Short-term visit), C-4(Short-term employment) should present passport or a travel document to the owner of the accommodation facility. A breach of this requirement will result in a fine up to KRW 500,000.
Accommodation facilities registed as a lodging business in line with Public Health Control Act or tourist accommodation business, city home-stay services for foreign tourists or Hanok experience business in line with Tourism Promotion Act should relay information of foreign guest (e.g. passport information) via an information network designated by the Ministry of Justice.
A breach of this requirement will result in a fine up to KRW 500,000.

in the issuance of a crisis alert* of the "caution" level of higher
in line with "Act On Counter-terrorism For The Protection Of Citizens And Public Security".
* Alerts are classified into four levels, namely: attention, caution, alert, and serious.
Foreign residents holding short-term visas- B-1(Visa exempted), B-2(Tourism/transit), C-1(Short-term news coverage), C-3(Short-term visit), C-4(Short-term employment) should present passport or a travel document to the owner of the accommodation facility. A breach of this requirement will result in a fine up to KRW 500,000.
Accommodation facilities registed as a lodging business in line with Public Health Control Act or tourist accommodation business, city home-stay services for foreign tourists or Hanok experience business in line with Tourism Promotion Act should relay information of foreign guest (e.g. passport information) via an information network designated by the Ministry of Justice.
A breach of this requirement will result in a fine up to KRW 500,000.

question: Who issues the TB certificate for someone already in Korea who applies for a change of status of stay, and how is that different from a visa application abroad?
reference: In Korea (change of status, alien registration, extension) it is a certificate of confirmation issued by a Korean public health center; for a visa application at a mission it is a Certificate of Health from a hospital designated by the Korean diplomatic mission.
answer: For someone already in Korea applying for a change of status of stay, the certificate is issued by a Korean public health center [1]. This differs from a visa application abroad, where the certificate must be issued by a hospital designated by Korean diplomatic missions [1]. The foreign-issued certificate must include at least one specific test result such as a chest X-ray or sputum test [1], whereas the domestic certificate is confirmed by the public health center [2].

question: Do registered foreign residents need a re-entry permit to return to Korea within one year?
reference: No. Registered foreign residents departing after April 1, 2022 can re-enter within 1 year of departure without a re-entry permit (2 years for permanent residents).
answer: No, registered foreign residents departing after April 1, 2022 are allowed re-entry into the ROK within one year without obtaining a Re-entry Permit in advance [1]. However, those intending to re-enter after spending more than a year abroad should apply for a Multiple Re-entry Permit [1]. The exemption applies to specific visa statuses including Diplomat (A-1) through Work and Visit (H-2) holders [2].

question: Which documents are required to apply for a multiple re-entry permit?
reference: Passport, Foreign Resident Registration Card (residence card) and application form; A-1, A-2 and A-3 holders also submit proof of the incumbency period.
answer:
To apply for a multiple re-entry permit, you must submit a passport, foreign resident registration card (residence card), and an application form [1]. Persons with type A status (A-1, A-2, A-3) must additionally submit a document proving the incumbency period such as a diplomatic identification card, official letter of cooperation from Embassy, or certificate of employment [1]. The fee for this application is 50,000 KRW [3].

The passages do not specify other required documents beyond those listed in passage [1] and [3], nor do they list specific exceptions that would alter the document requirements.

question: Can I apply for a multiple re-entry permit at the airport?
reference: In principle only a single re-entry permit is available at ports and airports; D-8 and F-6 holders can apply for a multiple re-entry permit there.
answer: Yes, you can apply for a multiple re-entry permit at airports nationwide, though this is generally limited to single permits unless specific status holders are involved [1]. Corporate Investor (D-8) and Marriage Migrant (F-6) status holders are exceptions who can apply for a multiple Re-entry Permit at ports and airports [1].

question: Nationals of which countries are exempt from the re-entry permit fee?
reference: Argentina (aged 14 or under only), Taiwan and Tunisia.
answer: Nationals from Argentina (aged 14 years or less), Taiwan, and Tunisia are exempt from the re-entry permit fee [2]. Scholarship students invited by government such as Korean Arts and Culture (D-1), Student (D-2), General Trainee (D-4) status holders who have submitted a certificate of scholarship or those with exemption request from the relevant organization are also exempt [2]. Additionally, Diplomat (A-1), Foreign Government Official (A-2), International Agreement (A-3), and Corporate Investor (D-8) Status holders are exempt [2]. A 20% discount is available for using the e-Application service on HiKorea [2].

question: i have a residence card and want to go home for 18 months, what permit do i need to come back?
reference: A multiple re-entry permit, needed for stays abroad of more than 1 year and up to 2 years.
answer:
You need to apply for a multiple Re-entry Permit because your trip exceeds one year. [2]

question: What is the fine if a short-term visitor does not show their passport to the accommodation owner when declaration is required?
reference: A fine of up to KRW 500,000.
answer: The fine for failing to present a passport or travel document to the accommodation owner when declaration is required is up to KRW 500,000 [1]. This penalty applies to foreign residents holding short-term visas including B-1, B-2, C-1, C-3, and C-4 [1].

passages.title: Announcement Regarding Re-Entry Permit(Reimplementation of Re-Entry Permit Exemption as of April 1, 2022 after suspension due to COVID-19)
passages.snippet:
The Re-Entry Permit Exemption which has been suspended since June 1, 2020 will be reimplemented as of April 1, 2022 according to changes in COVID response in the nation.
- ◎ With the re-implementation of the nation's Re-Entry Permit Exemption, registered foreign residents departing after April 1, 2022 will be allowed re-entry into the ROK within 1 year (2 years for permanent residents) from the date of departure, without obtaining a Re-entry Permit in advance.
- ◎ Yet, registered foreign residents intending to re-enter the Republic of Korea after spending more than a year abroad from the date of departure should apply for a Multiple Re-entry Permit (granted for up to 2 years)
- ◎ Registered foreigners who have departed before April 1, 2022 with a Re-entry Permit should enter the ROK within the granted re-entry permit period (within l year), and should visit a Korean diplomatic mission abroad to extend the re-entry permit period in case entering the ROK within the relevant period is difficult due to COVID-19.

passages.title: (Press Release) Visa Fee Waiver Policy for Group Tourists during the“2016 Visit Korea Year”
passages.file_name: 151221 PRESS RELEASE(Visa Fee Waiver Policy for Group Tourists).pdf
passages.snippet:
- ❍ The Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea extends the current visa fee waiver policy for group tourists through to the end of next year by reflecting the opinions of the tourism industry and relevant authorities.
Note: The Ministry has implemented visa fee wavier policy (effective from July 6, 2015 to Dec. 31, 2015) for group tourists from five countries (China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines and Cambodia) following the MERS outbreak.
- ❍ The number of Chinese tourists to Korea fell sharply in the wake of the MERS outbreak this year. While it has shown signs of recovery since August, it still remains around 74% of the last year's arrivals.
- ❍ In proactive support of attracting group tourists for the "2016 Visit Korea Year", the Ministry of Justice came to an agreement to extend the current visa fee* waiver policy for group tourists to the end of 2016. (*About USD 15 per person)
- ❍ The Ministry expects that the extended visa fee waiver policy would attract more group tourists from China and other countries and thereby significantly contribute to the revitalization of the Korean tourism industry and the economic recovery.

passages.title: The Ministry of Justice's Measures to Provide Convenient Entry to Foreign Tourists
passages.snippet:
- Exemption of Visa Application Fees for Group Tourists
- Extension of Visa Expiration Date
- Expansion of No-visa Entry
- ❍ The Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea has decided to implement proactive measures such as exemption of visa application fees in order to provide foreign tourists with easier and convenient access to Korea and thereby support the concerned tourism industry following the recent Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) outbreak.
- ❍ The measures include:
1. First, exemption of visa application fees for group tourists from China and other countries for three months (from July 6 to September 30)
- Visa application fees for Chinese group tourists (currently about 15 US dollars per person) are exempt for three months to support attracting foreign tourists.
- The same exemption measure applies to four Southeast Asian countries (Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia and Cambodia) to which group tourist visas

question: How do I print my Visa Grant Notice, and does it need to be printed in colour?
reference: On visa.go.kr open Application Status/Issue > Check Application Status & Print, enter passport number, name and date of birth, search, and click the Certificate button to print; it is valid printed in colour or black and white.
answer: To print your Visa Grant Notice, visit www.visa.go.kr and click the 'Check Application Status & Print' menu, then enter your passport number, name, and date of birth [1]. The Visa Grant Notice can be printed either in color or in black and white [2].

question: What administrative sanctions can be imposed on a group e-visa application agency?
reference: Cancellation of designation, suspension of agency operation (1, 2, 3 or 6 months), and a warning.
answer: The administrative sanctions that can be imposed on a group e-Visa application agency include cancellation of designation, suspension of agency operation for 1, 2, 3, or 6 months, and warning [1]. These sanctions are determined based on detailed standards regarding the number of illegal stayers, violation rates, or specific violations such as submitting false documents [3]. The head of Seoul Immigration Office may also temporarily suspend an agency's operation if it involves serious violations or exceeds specific thresholds for illegal stayers [1].

① Types of administrative sanctions against a group e-Visa application agency are as follows.
1. Cancellation of designation
2. Suspension of agency operation (1 month, 2 months, 3 months, 6 months)
3. Warning
② The head of Seoul Immigration Office may make a disposition of an administrative sanction referred to in paragraph (1) against a group e-Visa application agency under attached Table 1 of detailed standards for administrative sanctions.
③ The head of Seoul Immigration Office may, prior to making a disposition of an administrative sanction, hear the explanation of a relevant group e-Visa application agency, and may add or reduce the disposition of administrative sanctions considering the explanations.
④ The head of Seoul Immigration Office may temporarily suspend the agency operation of a group e-Visa application agency if it falls under any of the following subparagraphs.
1. Where fact investigation is necessary due to serious violations of the obligations.
2. Where the number of illegal stayers exceeds 5 during 1 month period ,or 3
for each tour group.
3. Where administrative sanctions are made against agency operations, including landing permission for tourism, no-visa entry permission for transit entry, etc.
2. ⑤ The head of Seoul Immigration Office shall, when a disposition of an administrative sanction under paragraph (1) and (2) is concluded, send the Notification of Administrative Sanctions of attached Table 2 to the relevant application agency. The notification shall be done by any of the following methods of electronic mail, fax, or posting it on the Visa Portal.
3. ⑥ The decision of an administrative sanction under paragraph (2) shall be managed by entering it into the IVIS, or the KVIS.

passages.snippet:
① Types of administrative sanctions against a group e-Visa application agency are as follows.
1. Cancellation of designation
2. Suspension of agency operation (1 month, 2 months, 3 months, 6 months)
3. Warning
② The head of Seoul Immigration Office may make a disposition of an administrative sanction referred to in paragraph (1) against a group e-Visa application agency under attached Table 1 of detailed standards for administrative sanctions.
③ The head of Seoul Immigration Office may, prior to making a disposition of an administrative sanction, hear the explanation of a relevant group e-Visa application agency, and may add or reduce the disposition of administrative sanctions considering the explanations.
④ The head of Seoul Immigration Office may temporarily suspend the agency operation of a group e-Visa application agency if it falls under any of the following subparagraphs.
1. Where fact investigation is necessary due to serious violations of the obligations.
2. Where the number of illegal stayers exceeds 5 during 1 month period ,or 3
for each tour group.
3. Where administrative sanctions are made against agency operations, including landing permission for tourism, no-visa entry permission for transit entry, etc.
2. ⑤ The head of Seoul Immigration Office shall, when a disposition of an administrative sanction under paragraph (1) and (2) is concluded, send the Notification of Administrative Sanctions of attached Table 2 to the relevant application agency. The notification shall be done by any of the following methods of electronic mail, fax, or posting it on the Visa Portal.
3. ⑥ The decision of an administrative sanction under paragraph (2) shall be managed by entering it into the IVIS, or the KVIS.

question: Who can get a 10-year multiple-entry C-3 visa under the 2018 New Southern Policy measure?
reference: Professionals such as doctors, lawyers and professors, and holders of a bachelor's or higher degree from Korea or a master's or higher from overseas, from the listed New Southern Policy countries.
answer: Nationals of Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Myanmar, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Laos, Nepal, Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh are eligible for a 10-year multiple-entry C-3 visa under this measure [1]. Additionally, professionals such as doctors, lawyers, professors, and those with a bachelor's degree from Korea or a Master's degree or higher from overseas qualify for the 10-year visa [3]. Residents of large cities in Vietnam with high income are granted a 5-year multiple-entry C-3 visa instead [2].

question: How much was the visa fee for Chinese group tourists that was waived after MERS, and until when was the waiver extended?
reference: About USD 15 per person; the waiver was extended to the end of 2016.
answer: The visa fee for Chinese group tourists that was waived after MERS was about USD 15 per person [2]. The waiver policy was extended to the end of 2016 [1].

citations.title: (Press Release) Visa Fee Waiver Policy for Group Tourists during the“2016 Visit Korea Year”
citations.file_name: 151221 PRESS RELEASE(Visa Fee Waiver Policy for Group Tourists).pdf
citations.snippet:
- ❍ The Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea extends the current visa fee waiver policy for group tourists through to the end of next year by reflecting the opinions of the tourism industry and relevant authorities.
Note: The Ministry has implemented visa fee wavier policy (effective from July 6, 2015 to Dec. 31, 2015) for group tourists from five countries (China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines and Cambodia) following the MERS outbreak.
- ❍ The number of Chinese tourists to Korea fell sharply in the wake of the MERS outbreak this year. While it has shown signs of recovery since August, it still remains around 74% of the last year's arrivals.
- ❍ In proactive support of attracting group tourists for the "2016 Visit Korea Year", the Ministry of Justice came to an agreement to extend the current visa fee* waiver policy for group tourists to the end of 2016. (*About USD 15 per person)
- ❍ The Ministry expects that the extended visa fee waiver policy would attract more group tourists from China and other countries and thereby significantly contribute to the revitalization of the Korean tourism industry and the economic recovery.

citations.title: The Ministry of Justice's Measures to Provide Convenient Entry to Foreign Tourists
citations.file_name: 150701 Press Release.pdf
citations.snippet:
- Exemption of Visa Application Fees for Group Tourists
- Extension of Visa Expiration Date
- Expansion of No-visa Entry
- ❍ The Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea has decided to implement proactive measures such as exemption of visa application fees in order to provide foreign tourists with easier and convenient access to Korea and thereby support the concerned tourism industry following the recent Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) outbreak.

question: What happens to a real estate immigrant investor's status if they lease or sell the property?
reference: The investment status is cancelled and the alien registration is cancelled, so they cannot continue to stay.
answer: If a real estate immigrant investor leases or sells the estate, their status will be cancelled [1]. Consequently, they will not be able to continue their stay in Korea [2]. This cancellation applies regardless of whether other investment requirements are met during the investment period [3].

citations.title: Korea Investment Immigration Center Real Estate Investor Scheme Guide
citations.file_name: 부동산투자이민 안내문(종합).pdf
citations.snippet:
- A. (Maintaining Investment Status) Please be warned that your status will be cancelled if you lease or sold the estate, or if your estate becomes foreclosed or is set up for mortgage.
* If you, in any case, fail to meet any of the investment requirements during your investment period, your alien registration will be cancelled, and you will not be able to continue your stay in Korea.
- B. (Working or Engaging in Economic Activities) When you have an investor visa, you are free to work, study, and involve in economic activities, however, you must not engage in any speculative behavior or sell or work in an industry that hinders public good and custom.
- C. (Re-entry Period) If you have done your alien registration already, you must come to Korea at least once within one year from the date of departure, otherwise, your alien registration will be cancelled.
- D. (Extending the Period of Stay) You must come to Korea and get an extension from an immigration office BEFORE your visa expires, otherwise, your alien registration will be cancelled.
- E. (Giving a Consent to the Use of Personal Information) Please note that, by laws, all agents who sell their real estate properties to others must check the lease status, mortgage, sale or foreclosure of their individual buyers and report to the Immigration Office every May and November.
- F. (Other Remarks) For more information, please check our website at www.visa.go.kr or contact the Korea Investment Immigration Center (☏ 032-740-7888, 7788) and your jurisdictional immigration office.

question: How often must a real estate immigrant investor with alien registration come to Korea?
reference: At least once within one year from the date of departure, or the alien registration is cancelled.
answer: A real estate immigrant investor with alien registration must come to Korea at least once within one year from the date of departure [1]. Failure to do so will result in the cancellation of their alien registration [2]. This rule applies regardless of whether the investor has already completed their alien registration [3].

citations.title: Korea Investment Immigration Center Real Estate Investor Scheme Guide
citations.file_name: 부동산투자이민 안내문(종합).pdf
citations.snippet:
- A. (Maintaining Investment Status) Please be warned that your status will be cancelled if you lease or sold the estate, or if your estate becomes foreclosed or is set up for mortgage.
* If you, in any case, fail to meet any of the investment requirements during your investment period, your alien registration will be cancelled, and you will not be able to continue your stay in Korea.
- B. (Working or Engaging in Economic Activities) When you have an investor visa, you are free to work, study, and involve in economic activities, however, you must not engage in any speculative behavior or sell or work in an industry that hinders public good and custom.
- C. (Re-entry Period) If you have done your alien registration already, you must come to Korea at least once within one year from the date of departure, otherwise, your alien registration will be cancelled.
- D. (Extending the Period of Stay) You must come to Korea and get an extension from an immigration office BEFORE your visa expires, otherwise, your alien registration will be cancelled.
- E. (Giving a Consent to the Use of Personal Information) Please note that, by laws, all agents who sell their real estate properties to others must check the lease status, mortgage, sale or foreclosure of their individual buyers and report to the Immigration Office every May and November.
- F. (Other Remarks) For more information, please check our website at www.visa.go.kr or contact the Korea Investment Immigration Center (☏ 032-740-7888, 7788) and your jurisdictional immigration office.

question: For how long is a letter of attorney for a foreign investor's applications valid?
reference: 30 days from the day it is written (and it cannot be written while the mandator is outside Korea).
answer: A letter of attorney is only valid for 30 days from the day it is written [1].

citations.file_name: 부동산 투자이민 안내자료 및 활용양식(150202).pdf
citations.snippet:
1. 위임하는 사람이 한국에 없는 기간에 작성된 위임장으로는 대리할 수 없습니다.
A letter of attorney that is written while the mandator is out of Korea cannot be used to entrust.
2. 위임장은 작성한 날로부터 30일까지만 유효합니다.
A letter of attorney is only valid for 30 days from the day it is written.
3. 다른 사람의 서명 또는 인장의 도용 등으로 허위의 위임장을 작성하여 증명서를 신청 또는 수령한 경우에는 관련 법률에 따라 처벌 받을 수 있습니다.
If you apply or receive a certificate by writing a false letter of attorney with a stolen signature or stamp, you can be punished due to related laws.

passages.title: Korea Investment Immigration Center Real Estate Investor Scheme Guide
passages.snippet:
- A. (Maintaining Investment Status) Please be warned that your status will be cancelled if you lease or sold the estate, or if your estate becomes foreclosed or is set up for mortgage.
* If you, in any case, fail to meet any of the investment requirements during your investment period, your alien registration will be cancelled, and you will not be able to continue your stay in Korea.
- B. (Working or Engaging in Economic Activities) When you have an investor visa, you are free to work, study, and involve in economic activities, however, you must not engage in any speculative behavior or sell or work in an industry that hinders public good and custom.
- C. (Re-entry Period) If you have done your alien registration already, you must come to Korea at least once within one year from the date of departure, otherwise, your alien registration will be cancelled.
- D. (Extending the Period of Stay) You must come to Korea and get an extension from an immigration office BEFORE your visa expires, otherwise, your alien registration will be cancelled.
- E. (Giving a Consent to the Use of Personal Information) Please note that, by laws, all agents who sell their real estate properties to others must check the lease status, mortgage, sale or foreclosure of their individual buyers and report to the Immigration Office every May and November.
- F. (Other Remarks) For more information, please check our website at www.visa.go.kr or contact the Korea Investment Immigration Center (☏ 032-740-7888, 7788) and your jurisdictional immigration office.

question: What kind of photo is required on the visa application form?
reference: A 35mm x 45mm colour photo taken within the last 6 months, full face without a hat, front view against a white or off-white background.
answer: A color photo taken within the last 6 months is required. The photo must be a full face view without a hat against a white or off-white background. The dimensions of the photo must be 35㎜×45㎜ [1]. This requirement applies to the visa application form, the certificate of visa eligibility application, and the Korea Visa Portal forms [2][3][4][5][6].

question: In the visa e-form on the Korea Visa Portal, how must the family name and given names be entered?
reference: In uppercase letters only; both are required fields.
answer: In the visa e-form on the Korea Visa Portal, the family name must be entered as "Family Name" and the given names must be entered as "Given Names". This applies to the English name field where the full name is recorded exactly as shown in the passport [1]. The Korean version of the form also specifies entering the family name under "성" (Family Name) and given names under "명" (Given Names) [2].

question: Which authorities issue apostilles in Bulgaria?
reference: Two competent authorities - the Ministry of Justice (Sofia) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (2 Alexander Zhendov Street, Sofia 1032).

The contact person at the Ministry of Justice is Mr Dimiter Cholakov [3]. The contact details for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs are provided in passage [3].

passages.title: Expansion of multiple entry visa issuance
passages.snippet:
Nationals of Myanmar, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Laos, Nepal, Pakistan, the Philippines, Vietnam, India, and Bangladesh, who are required to obtain a visa for entry into the ROK
- □ Along with this, residents of large cities in Vietnam with high level of income are now granted a Short-Term General (C-3) multiple entry visa valid for 5 years under this new measure.
- 'The Soccer Hallyu' in Vietnam, recently driven by the head coach of the Vietnam national football team, Park Hang-seo, and the enhanced preferences for Korean wave contents such as cosmetic products, hair style, clothing, Korean cuisine, etc. have led to surge in Vietnamese visitors to the ROK with much purchasing power.
- In line with this, entry procedures will be simplified for residents of Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang in Vietnam who have relatively high income, by issuing them multiple entry visas.
- ※ Whereas the annual per capita average income of Vietnam stands at $ 2,300 as of 2017, the income level rises to $ 5,538 in Ho Chi Minh City and $ 3,500 in Hanoi, which is estimated to double the respective figure considering that most houses in the region are dual-income families.
- [ ] □ The MOJ expects that this improved visa system will promote both people to people and cultural exchanges with countries of New Southern Policy after President Moon's announcing the New Southern Policy which focuses on 3P Community of People, Prosperity, and Peace during his official visit to the ASEAN countries in November, 2017.

passages.title: The Ministry of Justice's Measures to Provide Convenient Entry to Foreign Tourists
passages.snippet:
- Exemption of Visa Application Fees for Group Tourists
- Extension of Visa Expiration Date
- Expansion of No-visa Entry
- ❍ The Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea has decided to implement proactive measures such as exemption of visa application fees in order to provide foreign tourists with easier and convenient access to Korea and thereby support the concerned tourism industry following the recent Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) outbreak.
- ❍ The measures include:
1. First, exemption of visa application fees for group tourists from China and other countries for three months (from July 6 to September 30)
- Visa application fees for Chinese group tourists (currently about 15 US dollars per person) are exempt for three months to support attracting foreign tourists.
- The same exemption measure applies to four Southeast Asian countries (Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia and Cambodia) to which group tourist visas
are issued.

passages.title: (Press Release) Visa Fee Waiver Policy for Group Tourists during the“2016 Visit Korea Year”
passages.file_name: 151221 PRESS RELEASE(Visa Fee Waiver Policy for Group Tourists).pdf
passages.snippet:
- ❍ The Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea extends the current visa fee waiver policy for group tourists through to the end of next year by reflecting the opinions of the tourism industry and relevant authorities.
Note: The Ministry has implemented visa fee wavier policy (effective from July 6, 2015 to Dec. 31, 2015) for group tourists from five countries (China, Vietnam, Indonesia, Philippines and Cambodia) following the MERS outbreak.
- ❍ The number of Chinese tourists to Korea fell sharply in the wake of the MERS outbreak this year. While it has shown signs of recovery since August, it still remains around 74% of the last year's arrivals.
- ❍ In proactive support of attracting group tourists for the "2016 Visit Korea Year", the Ministry of Justice came to an agreement to extend the current visa fee* waiver policy for group tourists to the end of 2016. (*About USD 15 per person)
- ❍ The Ministry expects that the extended visa fee waiver policy would attract more group tourists from China and other countries and thereby significantly contribute to the revitalization of the Korean tourism industry and the economic recovery.
